grammar_choice.en_template: South Asian English refers to the varieties {{1:used/using}} in countries {{2:including/included}} India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 남아시아 영어는 인도, 파키스탄, 스리랑카를 포함한 나라들에서 쓰이는 변종들을 가리킨다.
explain: 변종은 "사용되는" 대상이므로 과거분사 used 가 맞다.
"~을 포함하여"라는 전치사 including 이 맞다.

grammar_choice.en_template: English {{1:was introduced/introduced}} to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century and {{2:reinforced/reinforcing}} by long-term British rule.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 영어는 17세기 초에 인도 아대륙에 도입되었고 장기간의 영국 통치에 의해 강화되었다.
explain: 영어는 "도입된" 대상이므로 수동태 was introduced 가 맞다.
was introduced 와 병렬된 수동태(was 생략)이므로 과거분사 reinforced 가 맞다.

grammar_choice.en_template: English {{1:is/are}} still used as an official language in {{2:some of the countries/some of the country}} in the region.

explain: 주어 English 가 단수이므로 is 가 맞다.
some of the 뒤에는 복수명사가 온다.

grammar_choice.en_template: For example, India {{1:has kept/has been kept}} English as an official language even after it became independent {{2:since/despite}} the country has hundreds of native languages aside from Hindi.

grammar_choice.en_template: For example, India has kept English as an official language even after it became independent since the country has {{1:hundreds of/hundred of}} native languages aside {{2:from/to}} Hindi.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 예를 들어 인도는 독립한 이후에도 영어를 공용어로 유지해 왔는데, 그 나라에는 힌디어 외에도 수백 개의 토착 언어가 있기 때문이다.

grammar_choice.en_template: The most popular variety of South Asian English {{1:is/are}} Indian English with about 125 {{2:million/millions}} speakers.

grammar_choice.en_template: It is sometimes {{1:called/calling}} "Hinglish," a mix of Hindi and English.

jumble.answer: South Asian English refers to the varieties used in countries including India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.
English was introduced to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century and reinforced by long-term British rule.
English is still used as an official language in some of the countries in the region.
For example, India has kept English as an official language even after it became independent since the country has hundreds of native languages aside from Hindi.
The most popular variety of South Asian English is Indian English with about 125 million speakers.
It is sometimes called "Hinglish," a mix of Hindi and English.
Indian English typically adds English words to Hindi; however, the meanings can change over time.
For instance, would-be in Indian English means "a fiancé" or "a fiancée," while airdash is the word for "travel hastily by plane."
It is sometimes called "Hinglish," a mix of Hindi and English.
